title: Graded endpoint failover contract and telemetry playbook for endpoint deprecation
creator: Liam Rodriguez
summary: Define a deterministic, metric-driven contract and playbook for graded failover when deprecating older inference endpoints. Aim is to minimize customer outages by specifying precise telemetry gates, TTLs for redirect/fallbacks, SLA adjustments during transitions, and client communications for phased migrations.
background: We are consolidating multiple inference transports (multiplexed streaming, legacy SSE, and polling) into the unified /v1/infer API over the next two quarters. Prior deprecation plans focused on timelines and compatibility shims; engineering has asked for a concrete, metric-driven failure contract so runtime can automatically trigger safe fallbacks (e.g., translated responses, limited-rate redirects, or temporary acceptance of older protocols) while minimizing load and cost. This ticket formalizes that contract and the telemetry gates that control automated failover behavior.
goals:
1) Provide clear SLO-adjusted failover modes and TTLs for up to 6 weeks post-deprecation.
2) Specify telemetry signals and threshold values that trigger automated downgrade/rollback.
3) Create a runbook for ops and SEs to coordinate client-facing rollouts and support.
4) Produce client guidance and SDK snippets for graceful retry/backoff and header hints.
non_goals:
1) Implementing the runtime failover code (owned by ENG tickets listed under dependencies).
2) Rewriting SDKs as part of this ticket (we will produce guidance and test vectors instead).
3) Replacing existing alerting targets — we will reference them but not migrate them here.
requirements:
- Define three graded failover tiers: advisory, limited-acceptance, and enforced-fallback, each with specific time windows and allowed degradation.
- For each tier, document exact telemetry gates: error-rate (5xx), client-error rate (4xx), QPS drop, median p99 latency, and KV cache miss amplification.
- TTLs and escalation: advisory (2 weeks), limited-acceptance (4 weeks), enforced-fallback (6 weeks) measured from official deprecation date.
- Provide per-customer opt-out and emergency rollback instructions tied to client's account id and dedicated capacity settings.
- Produce example SDK headers and compatibility-response schemas for the translation gateway.
- Acceptance criteria must be machine-checkable (dashboards and alert rules exist + runbook entries).
acceptance_criteria:
- Playbook doc exists and is linked in the Console runbook library.
- Dashboards with the described telemetry exist and show synthetic baseline test for at least 3 days.
- Automated gating rules described and documented; ENG dependencies have implementation PR numbers referenced.
- Customer-facing migration guide drafted and reviewed by Solutions/Support.
- Incident drill executed in staging that simulates enforced-fallback and validates rollback procedures.
telemetry_and_gates:
Primary signals: 5xx-rate (cluster-level and route-level), 4xx spike correlated with model alias mismatch, p99 latency increase > 2x baseline, KV cache evictions > 3x baseline, route QPS drop > 30% for 5m. Thresholds and gating logic:
- Advisory: any signal above threshold triggers internal Slack and OpsSRE paging; no automatic change.
- Limited-acceptance: sustained (10m) degradation of 2 signals triggers limited-acceptance mode: redirect up to 20% of traffic to translation gateway with rate-limits and caching.
- Enforced-fallback: sustained (30m) degradation of 3 signals triggers full enforced-fallback: translate and serve legacy payloads with telemetry tagging and reduced concurrency limits.
Telemetry outputs required: alert IDs, dashboard links, and synthetic test IDs. All gates must surface to the Console rollout UI as boolean flags.
rollout_plan:
1) Draft and review playbook with ENG/SRE/Support (2 weeks).
2) Add telemetry dashboard and gate prototypes in staging; run 72h synthetic tests (3 weeks).
3) Enable advisory mode in canary region for 1 week with 5 pilot customers (4 weeks).
4) Enable limited-acceptance globally after pilot sign-off and monitor 7 days.
5) After 6 weeks total from deprecation date, enforced-fallback may be enabled if rollback/opt-outs unresolved.
6) Post-mortem and lessons learned session within 1 week of any enforced-fallback activation.
communication_plan:
- Pre-deprecation: email + Console banner 45/30/14/7 days with link to migration guide and SDK hints.
- During advisory/limited-acceptance: targeted outreach from Solutions for affected customers and in-console notices.
- When enforced-fallback triggers: immediate status page update, postmortem flag, and customer-specific incident emails for Dedicated customers.
- Provide a shortcode and FAQ for common errors (403 on model alias, SSE reconnect guidance).

open_questions:
- What exact percent of traffic is acceptable for limited-acceptance per-customer? (default 20% proposed)
- Should Dedicated customers be exempt from enforced-fallback by default? (proposal: opt-out flag)
- How do we bill for translated responses during fallback windows — account against original vs. fallback model? Finance + Billing input required.
- Will KMS/HSM interactions during translation introduce new latency that invalidates our p99 gate assumptions?

2026-03-12: Agreed TTLs of 2/4/6 weeks after tradeoff session (PM + SRE) to balance customer migration time vs. operational cost.
